items.body:
## Finding

ADR-043 identifies scraped web/OSINT content as a primary indirect-prompt-injection distribution and describes agentic-loop routing tool results through governance. Current agentic-governance inputs are only `agent.task.*`, `agent.request.*`, and `agent.response.*`; `HandleToolResult` instead converts result content directly into a role=`tool` message and sends it in the next model request.

Evidence at `origin/main` `ad153b2000d2f1797fcba7446ed2a324ca546d35`:

- intended threat/flow: `docs/adr/043-prompt-injection-defense-detonation-corpus.md:9-47,210-220`
- current governance inputs: `processor/agentic-governance/config.go:185-219`; `processor/agentic-governance/component.go:308-337`
- direct tool-result context path: `processor/agentic-loop/handlers.go:2111-2181,2423-2478,2528-2570`
- full pre-truncation trajectory evidence: `processor/agentic-loop/handlers.go:2117,2130-2147`; `processor/agentic-loop/trajectory_evidence.go:22-96`

## Boundary

This issue owns classification/admission of untrusted result content before model consumption.

- #1045 separately owns making an already-produced governance verdict decodable and rule-readable; its three barriers do not create the missing `tool.result.*` ingestion path.
- #1049 owns preventing rule action templates from emitting opaque governance values; it matters only if disposition is rule-driven.
- #1058 owns booted E2E proof for the RuleReadable projection path if that path is claimed.
- #1033 shares the result-truncation seam; this issue must not re-derive truncation independently.
- #808 owns effect-derived approval of tool calls, not returned-content classification.
- #1006 owns non-Go dereference and authorization for stored evidence.
- #857 owns the systemic payload-size class and constrains any new result carrier.
- #1113 owns booted-binary E2E proof of existing web-observation entity birth.

#1045, #1049, and #1058 constrain a design that sends governance dispositions through rules. They do not block an inline classify/redact/block path before model context.

## Owner decisions required

- Whether governance blocks, redacts, annotates, or quarantines result content, and how shadow mode behaves.
- Whether the governed carrier is the existing result message, a derived bounded view, or another admitted contract.
- How full durable trajectory evidence is retained/access-controlled when model-visible content is altered or rejected.

## Acceptance

- Every external-content-producing builtin (`http_request`, `web_search`, bash URL fetches, and any future renderer) has a tested result-content governance path before model context.
- Missing/unavailable required governance fails closed or produces an explicit typed degraded state; it is not silent.
- Provenance and remote-content delimiters survive truncation/redaction.
- The solution preserves immutable completed tool outcomes and does not duplicate the adjacent owners listed above.

Owner accepted capturing this finding on 2026-08-27; detailed policy semantics remain `status:needs-decision`.

items.title: message_end safety send bypasses the source-coverage ledger and re-emits a delivered block
items.body:
## Summary

The message_end safety send re-emits a whole block that the streaming chunk path already delivered, because it does not consult the source-coverage ledger the chunk path uses.

Reproduced at `1a3d1cf2e14964db5baf6c3b92710c71d91b2872`:

```
src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.subscribe-embedded-agent-session.text-end-reconciliation.test.ts
  > text_end snapshot reconciliation
  > keeps native code continuation fenced after a shortened open-fence checkpoint
```

That test file is **byte-identical to `upstream/main`** (`git diff --stat upstream/main HEAD --` on it is empty), so this is our production failing upstream's own contract, not an adopted expectation we can re-point.

## Observed

Three fenced chunks are delivered correctly (each `<= maxChars` 20, each independently fenced). Then `message_end` emits a fourth:

```
"```txt\nabc\ndefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz\n```"
```

which is the whole code block reassembled — longer than the configured `maxChars`, and content the reader has already seen. The assertion that fails is the post-`message_end` one:

```ts
expect(extractTextPayloads(onBlockReply.mock.calls)).toEqual(delivered);
```

## Root cause

`emitBlockChunk` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.stream-rendering.ts` maintains a **source-coordinate** coverage ledger and refuses an emission whose source range is already covered:

- `coveredBlockSources` (`stream-rendering.ts:133`), populated at `:618` from the emitted `blockSourceRange`
- consulted as `sourceRangeAlreadyCovered` (`:453`)

The `message_end` safety send in `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.lifecycle.ts` does not go through `emitBlockChunk`. It calls `ctx.emitBlockReply` directly, carries no `sourceStart`/`sourceEnd`, and therefore never consults coverage. Its only duplicate guards are text comparisons:

```ts
} else if (finalAssistantText !== textEndDeliveredVisibleText || finalDirectives.hasMetadata) {
```

Those comparisons are against the **delivered display ledger**, whose entries carry presentation scaffolding that canonical text does not have. Here the scaffolding is the chunker's *synthetic* fences (each chunk is re-fenced so it stands alone as markdown), so no entry can be found inside canonical, `deliveredCanonicalPrefix` bails, and `resolveFinalReplyReconciliation` falls through to its whole-message fallback:

```ts
} else if (params.finalAssistantText !== textEndDeliveredVisibleText) {
  finalTextCorrection = params.finalAssistantText;
}
```

This is the third distinct instance of that same fallback misfiring. Its own comment already documents the first (`"First "` vs `"First\nSecond"`, cured by retrying the prefix test against the trimmed delivered text), and `5f9c89029c` cured the second (`[tool calls omitted]` placeholder lines, cured by projecting the ledger through the same user-facing filter that produced canonical). Each cure removed one alphabet mismatch. The fallback keeps finding new ones because comparing *projected display text* against *canonical display text* is the wrong basis for "has the reader seen these source bytes".

## Proposed fix

Gate the `message_end` safety send on the same source-coverage ledger the chunk path already uses, rather than adding a fourth string normalization. Concretely: give the safety send the source coordinates of the text it is about to re-send and route it through (or consult) `sourceRangeAlreadyCovered`, so a fully covered source range cannot be re-emitted whatever the display alphabet looks like.

Explicitly **not** `blockChunker.consumedLength`: that field documents `"Prepared source boundaries are not evidence that a recipient received a chunk."` (`embedded-agent-block-chunker.ts:196`). `coveredBlockSources` is populated on actual emission and is the delivery-grounded ledger.

## Not a regression from the #1380 cures

Verified by reverting `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/sanitize-user-facing-text.ts` and `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.final-reconciliation.ts` to their pre-cure state and re-running: **2 failed / 54 passed either way**. The cures neither caused nor masked this.

## Classification

This is the only known red left in the `agents-core` surface at the assembly candidate after the twelve `src/auto-reply/reply` regressions in #1380 were cured. Recording it so a proof corpus taken at this SHA is labelled honestly rather than presented as clean.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01Fq5EX9ESA3CG9cuZxVoKAK

items.title: [Feature / Bug]: Combo fallback is bypassed on HTTP 200 `content_filter` / safety refusals (Anthropic ToS blocks)
items.body:
**9Router fails to trigger model combo fallback when upstream providers return HTTP 200 with safety refusals (`finish_reason: "content_filter"` / `stop_reason: "refusal"`), causing automated workflows to abort fatally instead of failing over to subsequent combo targets.**

To solve this, 9Router's combo execution loop needs to evaluate response completion metadata (`finish_reason === 'content_filter'` / provider refusal payloads) alongside HTTP status codes when determining candidate failure.

---

## Related Issues

### In `decolua/9router`
- **Issue #3136**: *Feature Request/Bug: Implement rotation/fallback stream stall detection* — Highlights that 9Router fallback only triggers on initial transport failures / HTTP error status codes, missing in-stream failure modes.
- **Issue #2467**: *Feature Request: Priority-Based Combo Strategy with Automatic Fallback* — Defines prioritized provider fallback requirements during provider limits and outages.
- **Issue #1641**: *Auto retry issue on quota/status exhaustion* — Documents candidate failure categorization and transition into combo fallback.

### Upstream Ecosystem References
- **`anthropics/claude-code#95670`**: *[Bug] Safeguard blocks firing on all requests with identical prompt templates (reasoning_extraction / duplicate model outputs)*.
- **`simonw/llm-anthropic#90`**: *Handle Fable refusals: Claude refused this request (`reasoning_extraction` / Terms of Service)*.

---

## Problem Description

When using a fallback combo (e.g., `genius` configured with `[cc/claude-sonnet-5-5(high), cx/gpt-6-astra(high)]`), 9Router currently checks whether upstream returns HTTP 4xx (e.g. 429) or 5xx. If so, it logs `[COMBO] Trying model 2/N` and fails over.

However, providers like Anthropic return heuristic safeguard blocks (such as multi-agent burst detection tripping `reasoning_extraction`) as an **HTTP 200 OK** payload containing:
```json
{
  "choices": [
    {
      "finish_reason": "content_filter",
      "index": 0,
      "message": {
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": "This request was blocked as it seems to violate Anthropic's Terms of Service restrictions on reverse engineering or duplicating model outputs. To learn more, visit https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms."
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
Or native Anthropic Messages API:
```json
{
  "type": "message",
  "stop_reason": "refusal",
  "stop_details": { "type": "content_filter", "category": "reasoning_extraction" },
  "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "This request was blocked as it seems to violate Anthropic's Terms of Service..." }]
}
```

Because the HTTP status is 200, 9Router logs:
```text
[COMBO] Model cc/claude-sonnet-5-5 succeeded
```
It immediately flushes this refusal downstream. Client agents (OpenCode, Claude Code, Cursor, Cline) treat the response as a terminal provider refusal and crash or stop the session, completely ignoring the second model in the combo (`cx/gpt-6-astra`).

---

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Define a 9Router fallback combo with two distinct providers:
   ```json
   {
     "id": "test-fallback",
     "name": "Test Fallback",
     "strategy": "fallback",
     "models": [
       "cc/claude-sonnet-5-5",
       "cx/gpt-6-astra"
     ]
   }
   ```
2. Send a request to `http://localhost:20128/v1/chat/completions` pointing to model `test-fallback`.
3. Simulate or trigger an upstream Anthropic content/ToS filter response (HTTP 200 with `finish_reason: "content_filter"`).
4. **Observed Behavior:** 9Router marks `cc/claude-sonnet-5-5` as succeeded, forwards the content filter message to the caller, and never attempts `cx/gpt-6-astra`.
5. **Expected Behavior:** 9Router detects `finish_reason: "content_filter"` / `stop_reason: "refusal"`, marks candidate 1 as failed, and falls back to candidate 2 (`cx/gpt-6-astra`).

---

## Root Cause Analysis

In 9Router's proxy layer:
1. Candidate success is evaluated solely on `response.ok` (HTTP status code `200-299`).
2. Neither the non-streaming JSON body nor the opening chunks of a streaming SSE response are inspected for provider-level refusal finish reasons.
3. The combo router lacks an evaluation hook to treat `content_filter` / `refusal` as a retriable failure condition.

---

## Proposed Solution

### 1. Non-Streaming Requests
In the combo execution handler, after parsing the upstream JSON body:
```typescript
const isContentFilter = 
  data?.choices?.[0]?.finish_reason === "content_filter" ||
  data?.stop_reason === "refusal" ||
  data?.stop_details?.type === "content_filter";

if (isContentFilter && combo.fallbackOnContentFilter !== false) {
  logger.warn(`[COMBO] Model ${model} returned content_filter/refusal. Failing over to next candidate.`);
  // Trigger next candidate in combo loop instead of returning 200 to client
  continue;
}
```

### 2. Streaming (SSE) Requests
Anthropic and OpenAI send `content_filter` either:
- In the initial response payload before text generation starts, or
- As an immediate single-event block (`message_start` followed directly by `message_delta` with `stop_reason: "refusal"` and 0 tokens of generated code).

**Implementation:**
- Buffer the stream until the first substantive delta or terminal stop reason event before piping headers to the downstream client.
- If the stream terminates immediately with `finish_reason: "content_filter"` and zero valid completion output, abort the stream upstream without flushing to client, increment combo candidate index, and route to the next provider.

### 3. Combo Configuration Setting (Opt-in / Configurable)
Add a flag to combo options so users can control whether content filters trigger fallback:
```json
{
  "id": "genius",
  "strategy": "fallback",
  "fallbackOnContentFilter": true,
  "models": ["cc/claude-sonnet-5-5(high)", "cx/gpt-6-astra(high)"]
}
```

---

## Environment
- **9Router Version**: `v0.5.65` / `v0.5.91`
- **Clients Tested**: OpenCode CLI, Antigravity
- **Affected Models**: `cc/*` (Claude Code OAuth proxy) failing over to `cx/*` (Codex)

items.title: W2-P0: Implement finite stochastic kernels, Bayes filter and temporal-law counterexample
items.body:
## Goal
Turn the accepted-to-review **proposed RFC-007** mathematical design into a dependency-light, falsifiable Python reference implementation. This is the **next coding step**, not a claim that MathKernel already exists.

**Source and specifications:** [RFC-007](https://github.com/CocAgent/OpenWorld/blob/main/docs/math/RFC-007-OPENWORLD-MATHEMATICAL-FOUNDATIONS.md), [Implementation Gates](https://github.com/CocAgent/OpenWorld/blob/main/docs/math/MATHKERNEL-P0-IMPLEMENTATION-GATES.md), parent W2 issue #3, W0 RFC-006, W5 verification #11.

## Deliverables
1. Pure finite controlled Markov kernels, rigorous finite row-stochastic validation, composition and identity operations.
2. Discrete POMDP Bayesian update with explicit error when evidence probability is zero.
3. Mathematically transparent two-sign Markov chain counterexample: q=0.9 and q=0.1 share one-time marginals but have different lag-one joint dependence.
4. A scoped predictive-sufficiency experiment: define task family, action/observation model, horizon and distortion. Test an exact-history query that the compact state *cannot* answer; return UNAVAILABLE.
5. Versioned reference fixtures, deterministic tests and clear import/API compatibility with W0.

## Acceptance tests
- [ ] Kernel non-negativity, finiteness and row sums; reject NaN and unknown supports
- [ ] Identity and associativity to a declared floating tolerance
- [ ] Hand-calculated two-state Bayes posterior, zero evidence error
- [ ] Marginal-equality / temporal-dependence inequality counterexample
- [ ] Task-bounded sufficiency statement with a deliberate failing exact query
- [ ] Local tests executed against the exact head and merged main SHAs
- [ ] Independent W5 reproducibility and security gate #11 not bypassed
- [ ] No real user data, costly external APIs, unreviewed old ZIPs or production deployment

## Scope and dependencies
Paths: `src/openworld_superkernel/math_*`, `tests/test_math_*`, `docs/math/`. Branch prefix: `feat/math-kernel-finite`. English only. Prefer standard-library Python and numerical fixtures. Do **not** bring in heavy RL/category theory frameworks for P0.

## Research and safety boundaries
This task demonstrates finite reference mathematics. It does **not** prove general agent intelligence, universally sufficient memory, safety in production, or large-scale social-agent performance. W0's proposed provenance/consent invariants remain binding design constraints.

**Suggested review:** independent mathematics review + W5 reproduction, then owner merge approval.

items.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When compaction summarization hits Google's `PROHIBITED_CONTENT` / `PROMPT_BLOCKED` safety block, the error is not classified as a failover reason, so the configured `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` chain is never attempted and compaction dies on the primary Gemini model even when non-Google fallbacks would summarize the transcript successfully.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On OpenClaw main HEAD (`05a86bd226d`), configure `agents.defaults.model.primary` = `google/gemini-3.8-flash` (or any Gemini) with `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` including a non-Google entry (e.g. `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, `nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b`).
2. Build up a session transcript that trips Google's `PROHIBITED_CONTENT` safety filter (real user transcript, ~688 messages in this repro).
3. Trigger `/compact` from Telegram (or any surface that runs the safeguard compaction pipeline).
4. Observe compaction fails immediately with `Compaction safeguard could not summarize the session: … Google prompt blocked (PROHIBITED_CONTENT) | summarization_failed`, with no attempt made against the non-Google fallbacks.

### Expected behavior

Per `resolveCompactionFallbacksOverride` at `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.ts:200-213`, compaction inherits the agent's `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` chain when the primary model fails. A provider-side safety block that is inherent to that provider (not the transcript) should be treated as a failover-eligible failure so the chain is exercised and a non-Google fallback can complete the summary.

### Actual behavior

- `packages/ai/src/providers/google-stream.ts:207-212` throws with `{ code: blockReason, type: "google_prompt_blocked" }` (e.g. `code: "PROHIBITED_CONTENT"`).
- `src/agents/failover/classify.ts` and `src/agents/failover/classify-core.ts` contain no mapping for `google_prompt_blocked` / `PROHIBITED_CONTENT` / `PROMPT_BLOCKED` (grep returns no matches on main HEAD).
- Consequently `resolveFailoverReasonFromError` returns `null` → `coerceToFailoverError` returns `null` at `src/agents/failover-error.ts:594-659` → `classifyCompactionFallbackResult` at `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.ts:221-239` returns `null` → the fallback runner is never invoked for this failure class.
- User-visible surface is the safeguard's terminal cancel at `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.ts:1429-1445`.

### OpenClaw version

main HEAD `05a86bd226d` (3238 commits ahead of the latest release tag `v2026.9.5`; `package.json` on main still reads `2026.9.5` but that is not the released version)

### Operating system

macOS 12.7.6 (build 21H1320)

### Install method

pnpm dev / source checkout of main

### Model

`google/gemini-3.8-flash` (primary), with non-Google fallbacks configured

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> google (Generative Language API)

### Additional provider/model setup details

```jsonc
// agents.defaults (redacted)
{
  \"model\": {
    \"primary\": \"google/gemini-3.8-flash\",
    \"fallbacks\": [
      \"google/gemini-3.7-flash\",
      \"google/gemini-3.6-flash\",
      \"nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b\",
      \"openai/gpt-5.6-luna\"
      // ...
    ]
  },
  \"compaction\": { \"mode\": \"safeguard\" }  // no compaction.model override
}
```

### Logs

```shell
Compaction failed: Compaction safeguard could not summarize the session:
All summarization attempts failed for 688 messages.
Last error: Summarization failed: Google prompt blocked (PROHIBITED_CONTENT) | summarization_failed
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

- Affected: users whose primary compaction model is a Google/Gemini model and whose transcripts contain content Gemini's safety filter blocks.
- Severity: blocks workflow — no way to compact the session; user must manually swap primary model or set an `agents.defaults.compaction.model` override.
- Frequency: deterministic once a transcript trips the safety filter.
- Consequence: session cannot compact, context saturates, agent effectively wedged for that session.

### Additional information

Suggested fix location: add `google_prompt_blocked` (and equivalent OpenAI/Anthropic content-policy signals if desired) to the failover classification in `src/agents/failover/classify.ts` so the fallback chain is exercised for provider-side safety refusals. Workaround for affected users: set `agents.defaults.compaction.model` to a non-Google model (single-string override at `src/config/zod-schema.agent-defaults-base.ts:202`).


---

**Update 2026-10-08 — still reproducible on `main`** (v2026.10.1-beta.2 @ `e73b64b7f62`):

- `packages/ai/src/providers/google-stream.ts:190,196` still throws `{ code: blockReason, type: "google_prompt_blocked" }` on `PROHIBITED_CONTENT` / `PROMPT_BLOCKED`.
- `git grep -E 'google_prompt_blocked|PROHIBITED_CONTENT|PROMPT_BLOCKED|prompt_blocked' origin/main -- 'src/agents/failover/'` returns zero matches — no classifier mapping has been added.
- `classifyCoreFailoverReasonFromErrorType` in `src/agents/failover/classification-rules.ts` still only handles `invalid_request_error`, `server_error`, `upstream_error`, `overloaded_error`; no case for `google_prompt_blocked`.
- Downstream behaviour unchanged: `coerceToFailoverError` returns `null` → `classifyCompactionFallbackResult` returns `null` → the configured `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` chain is never invoked, compaction dies on the primary Gemini model.

items.title: [Research] Adaptive privacy-loss filters for agent observation and evidence release
items.body:
# Research idea: adaptive privacy-loss filters for agent observation and evidence release

## Background / problem

The repository has provenance and information-flow control (#5333), evidence compression (#5329), and observation/causal attribution (#5323), but it does not yet treat repeated observation itself as a consumable privacy resource. An agent can make many adaptive screenshots, OCR queries, tool calls, or evidence disclosures; each may be individually authorized while their composition reveals sensitive user state. A static permission check or one-time redaction does not account for adaptive query history.

## Source and what it establishes

- Dwork, *Differential Privacy*, ICALP 2006, DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/11787006_1. The work introduces differential privacy as a bound on the increased risk caused by an individual's participation in a dataset.
- Rogers, Roth, Ullman, and Vadhan, *Privacy Odometers and Filters: Pay-as-you-Go Composition*, NeurIPS 2016, arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.08294. The paper distinguishes an adaptive privacy filter, which stops interaction before a target budget is exceeded, from an odometer, which tracks realized privacy loss when query count and parameters are adaptive.
- Whitehouse, Ramdas, Rogers, and Wu, *Fully-Adaptive Composition in Differential Privacy*, ICML 2023, PMLR: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/whitehouse23a.html. The paper tightens filters and odometers for fully adaptive composition, where both algorithms and privacy parameters depend on prior outcomes.

These sources establish formal composition accounting for privacy loss. They do not establish that UI screenshots, tool traces, or agent evidence can be assigned valid differential-privacy mechanisms or that noise is acceptable for safety-critical interface decisions.

## Structural analogy

| Differential-privacy composition | agent-interface analogue |
|---|---|
| adaptive query to a dataset | screenshot/OCR/state query or evidence request chosen from prior observations |
| privacy loss parameter | incremental exposure of user data, secrets, or sensitive UI state |
| privacy filter | admission gate that stops, redacts, coarsens, or asks for consent before further observation |
| privacy odometer | auditable cumulative exposure ledger with a confidence bound |
| neighboring datasets | neighboring user states differing in one sensitive fact or UI element |
| utility/privacy tradeoff | task progress or evidence quality versus disclosure risk |

The shared structure is adaptive interaction with a hidden state, where individually bounded observations compose over time. The analogy breaks because privacy loss is not automatically measurable from pixels, and adding noise can destroy action correctness or safety evidence.

## Proposed idea

Introduce an observation/evidence privacy contract with:

- a sensitivity class for each observation route (pixel, OCR, window title, clipboard, tool result, evidence bundle);
- an adaptive privacy-loss estimate or conservative symbolic cost;
- a filter that stops or changes modality when a declared budget is reached;
- an odometer that records realized exposure, confidence, user consent, and recipient scope;
- explicit exceptions for safety-critical observations, with compensating controls rather than silent bypass;
- a separation between private raw evidence and a minimized public proof/predicate.

The first implementation can avoid claiming formal DP for pixels. It can compare symbolic exposure budgets, interval bounds, and a redaction/predicate-only policy on synthetic neighboring UI states. A later phase can map selected routes to actual DP mechanisms only where their assumptions hold.

## Novelty check

- All-state repository title search for `privacy|private|differential|leak|confidential|redact|data minim|information flow` found no direct research Issue (only an unrelated closed private-Xvfb successor).
- #5333 governs provenance-labeled information flow and authority boundaries; this proposal adds adaptive cumulative exposure accounting and a stop/odometer distinction.
- #5329 compresses evidence under bounded interfaces; compression may reduce exposure but is not a privacy guarantee or an adaptive budget mechanism.
- #5323 separates observation, intervention, and causal attribution; it supplies a useful route taxonomy but does not account for disclosure composition.
- Differential privacy and privacy odometers are established prior art. The candidate novelty is applying adaptive composition concepts to agent observation/evidence routes while explicitly refusing unjustified DP claims for arbitrary GUI data.

## H/T/D/C/U

- **H**: An adaptive observation privacy filter reduces sensitive-state exposure and repeated disclosure relative to static per-call authorization, while preserving more useful task progress than a global deny-all policy.
- **T**: Create neighboring synthetic UI states differing in one sensitive element. Generate adaptive observation policies that choose the next route from prior outputs. Compare static authorization, global budget, symbolic odometer/filter, and predicate-only release. Measure exposure distinguishability, useful completion, evidence sufficiency, consent prompts, and false denials.
- **D**: PASS only if the filter enforces its declared exposure bound under adaptive traces, logs every budget decision, and does not silently reveal the sensitive difference; FAIL if adaptive composition exceeds the bound, if safety-critical exceptions bypass accounting, or if the policy claims DP without a valid mechanism proof. UNCERTAIN if sensitivity or neighboring-state assumptions are not auditable.
- **C**: If accounting is too weak to be meaningful, route-specific capability and manual consent may be the only defensible control. If privacy-preserving evidence destroys task correctness, the system may need to separate private execution from public proof instead of perturbing observations.
- **U**: Differential privacy assumes a formal randomized mechanism and a well-defined neighboring relation; arbitrary screenshots and tool outputs do not satisfy this automatically. User expectations, secret correlation, side channels, model memorization, and cross-session linkage are not captured by a toy budget.

## Minimal verification

Freeze a synthetic UI generator, neighboring-state definition, observation routes, adaptive policy, exposure accounting rule, seeds, and distinguisher. Emit raw JSONL query/output traces, budget deltas, filter/odometer decisions, redactions, consent events, and final exposure estimates. Independently replay the policy and run the distinguisher on neighboring states. Treat symbolic accounting as exploratory evidence until a valid mechanism-specific privacy proof exists.

## Expected value / roadmap connection

This connects observation gating, evidence compression, information-flow control, user-facing consent, and bounded interfaces. It challenges the assumption that an authorized observation remains harmless when repeated adaptively: the relevant resource may be cumulative disclosure rather than a single capability check.

## Cost / risk

The synthetic experiment is low cost and model-free. Production work requires sensitivity classification, route instrumentation, privacy accounting, redaction/predicate design, and policy for safety exceptions. Main risks are false DP claims, over-redaction that prevents safe operation, unmodeled side channels, and confusing a symbolic exposure score with a formal privacy guarantee.

items.title: [CI][P2] Limit superseded PR workflow fan-out without weakening required Windows safety checks
items.body:
## Evidence (read-only review, 10-20-2026)

- GitHub Actions API reports **1,376 workflow runs** in this repository. This is a lifetime counter, **not** an estimate of billed minutes or current cost.
- The latest 100 runs span **10-18-2026 04:06–04:50 UTC**. Of these, **77** are `pull_request` runs across six separate workflows, plus `push` runs for several workflows. This is high dispatch volume for a short interval; the source of individual updates should be confirmed before assuming wasted billing.
- All six checked files in [`.github/workflows/`](https://github.com/Cucklord420/MRI-Drive-Maker/tree/main/.github/workflows) declare `pull_request:` without path filtering and **none** declares `concurrency:` (top-level or job-level): `powershell.yml`, `rust-manifest.yml`, `rust-path-safety.yml`, `rust-release.yml`, `rust-safety.yml`, `static-analysis.yml`.
- Several also run on feature-branch `push`, so the same commit can queue overlapping CI while its pull request is open.

## Requested change (PR only; preserve safety coverage)

1. Record the six workflows' required-check status and actual run-minute/billing impact first. Do not classify failures or costs from `total_count` alone.
2. Add **PR-scoped** concurrency grouping/cancellation of superseded runs where safe; never cancel protected-branch, release, or intentionally manual safety/acceptance runs.
3. Avoid redundant `push` + `pull_request` checks for the same change where possible. If introducing path-aware work, preserve always-reported required status checks; do **not** deadlock protected PRs with workflow-level `paths` filters.
4. Preserve Windows storage safety, original-vs-Rust parity, packaging verification, and static analysis for every relevant change; run the appropriate checks on a revision before/after the configuration change.
5. Verify on a test PR with repeated pushes that superseded runs are cancelled, the final commit's required checks report correctly, and no release/manual validation was skipped. Document the measured run-count/minute difference.

**Scope:** CI dispatch efficiency only; no change to destructive USB behavior or bypass of safeguards. No repository changes made in this audit.

Related technical reference examined via Stack Overflow for Agents: path-filtered required-check deadlock mechanics and multi-agent CI fan-out. These are supporting heuristics, not measurements of this repository's billed usage.

## PR overlap and verification — 10-20-2026

Open PR #29 already adds cancellation of superseded Rust validation runs. Review its exact workflow coverage against the six triggered workflows before implementing this issue; avoid a duplicate competing concurrency PR. Independently establish required-check branch protection, avoid cancellation of release/manual acceptance runs, and measure check dispatch/run-minutes on a controlled candidate. No billed-minute or cost savings have been proven by the run-count statistic alone.

items.title: [Story] Backend: evaluate and persist a policy decision for every agent cycle
items.body:
**As an auditor, I want every agent cycle to carry a persisted, queryable policy decision, so that the decision timeline and audit history always show why a proposal passed or failed.**

**Why / context:** Today `evaluate_policies` runs only on the AUTO execution path and at approval time (`app/agent/approval.py evaluate_and_submit_cycle_trade`). For HOLD / OBSERVE_ONLY / REQUIRED(pending) cycles, no policy evaluation is persisted, so `snapshot_json["policy_evaluation"]` is empty — which leaves the decision timeline (#81) and audit filter-by-policy (#82) hollow. This completes #69's "store … policies."

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every actionable cycle records a `PolicyDecision` (ALLOW/DENY + per-policy PASS/FAIL/NA + evidence), OR an explicit `NOT_EVALUATED` marker when evaluation is intentionally skipped (e.g. a pure HOLD).
- The policy result is persisted in a queryable form on `AgentCycle` (a dedicated column/table, not only inside `snapshot_json`) to support #82's "filter by policy."
- No change to the safety gates: the persisted audit record must not weaken or bypass the existing execution-time evaluation.

## Proposed Implementation
- In `run_agent_cycle` (`app/agent/orchestrator.py`), after a valid proposal, build the `PolicyContext` (as `approval.py` already does) and call `evaluate_policies` for audit — OR record `NOT_EVALUATED` for HOLD. Keep it deterministic.
- Persist a `policy_decision` (Enum `PolicyDecisionType`) + `policy_result_json` column on `AgentCycle` (`app/db/models.py`); surface via `CycleRead`. Note: no Alembic today (schema via `ensure_*` in `app/db/schema.py`); a proper migration is M1/#85.
- Keep the authoritative execution-time evaluation in `evaluate_and_submit_cycle_trade` unchanged — this adds an audit record, it does not replace the gate.

## Tests
- `test_non_auto_cycle_persists_policy_record` — a HOLD/pending cycle persists a `PolicyDecision` (or explicit `NOT_EVALUATED`) queryable on `AgentCycle`.
- `test_auto_cycle_still_evaluates_and_submits` — the AUTO path is unchanged (evaluate + submit as today).
- `test_persisted_policy_queryable_by_outcome` — cycles can be selected by "policy X == FAIL" (supports #82's filter-by-policy).
- `test_audit_record_does_not_bypass_execution_gate` — adding the audit record does not alter or skip the execution-time evaluation/gate.

## Definition of Done
- Every actionable cycle records a queryable policy result (or `NOT_EVALUATED`) on `AgentCycle`, surfaced via `CycleRead`.
- The execution-time evaluation in `evaluate_and_submit_cycle_trade` is unchanged and still authoritative.
- The tests above pass; the new column is added (migration handled under M1/#85).

## Dependencies / relationships
- **Depends on:** nothing.
- **Blocks:** #81 (timeline), #82 (audit filter-by-policy). **Completes** #69.
- **Alt:** could be absorbed into #69 (expand its scope).

## Open question
- Should HOLD cycles run `evaluate_policies` for completeness, or record `NOT_EVALUATED`? Deterministic either way; decide alongside #81/#82.

_Target milestone: Sprint 3 (baseline — the application functions end-to-end)._

items.title: [Research] Deadline-constrained minimum spacing for safety reassessments
items.body:
## Status / type

**Transfer idea — unverified.** This is a bounded finite-model research proposal, not a runtime scheduler, safety certificate, allocation, or claim about live GUI/DOOM behavior.

## Source and what it actually establishes

Taylor, Ong, Cortés & Ames, “Safety-Critical Event Triggered Control via Input-to-State Safe Barrier Functions,” *IEEE Control Systems Letters* 5(3), 749–754 (2021), DOI: [10.1109/LCSYS.2020.3005101](https://doi.org/10.1109/LCSYS.2020.3005101); [author manuscript](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.06963).

Under its stated continuous-time dynamics, safe-set, measurement-error, and barrier-function assumptions, the paper gives an event-triggered safety construction with uniformly lower-bounded inter-event times. It also shows why a direct safety-trigger transcription can lack a minimum inter-event time near the safe-set boundary. It does **not** establish a sampling policy for arbitrary GUIs, discrete event queues, or unknown agent effects.

## Problem

The repository has separate strands for critical-event retention under planner backpressure (#658/#668/#712/#1008/#1021), optional producer throttling (#6650 and controller-law successor #6710), hazard-aware local action horizons (#6089/#5905/#5317), and planner/local-mode hysteresis (#5352). A remaining integration-shaped question is how a bounded controller should schedule repeated *safety reassessments* when a risk signal is noisy or approaches a boundary while planner service is delayed: unlimited retriggers can consume the observation/verifier budget and starve other work, while a fixed refractory interval can miss a rapidly closing deadline.

## Structural analogy and its limit

In event-triggered safety control, measurement error and distance to the safety boundary determine when a controller must update; the proof also constrains how close successive update events can be. Here, an already-authorized local-control lease has a risk/deadline margin and bounded observation→decision→release latency. That margin could determine an earliest safe next reassessment time, while a hard invalidation/revocation event remains an immediate bypass.

Common structure: evolving partially observed state, costly updates, a safety boundary, delayed actuation/release, and competing update-rate versus safety costs. Non-analogy: GUI/agent state is discrete, semantic, and often not governed by known dynamics or a differentiable barrier. Therefore no continuous-control guarantee transfers; the first rung must use an explicit finite state/uncertainty model and label all assumptions.

## Proposed idea: deadline-constrained event spacing

For each bounded local-control lease, define in a frozen model: a risk-margin bucket; an uncertainty-growth bound; worst-case capture, verifier, dispatch, and physical-release delays; optional-observation budget; and a hard set of events that bypass all pacing (lease invalidation, focus/target loss, explicit revoke, mandatory safety event). Choose the next *optional* reassessment time as the latest time whose worst-case margin still exceeds total response latency plus uncertainty reserve, but no earlier than a declared minimum event spacing. If those constraints conflict, the selector must immediately yield/release rather than silently stretch the deadline. Do not infer “safe” from an absent or untrackable event.

This differs from ordinary hysteresis (#5352): it schedules when optional reassessment may occur against a bounded reaction deadline; it does not filter mode transitions. It differs from #6650: its controlled variable is the spacing of repeated safety reassessments within an active lease, not generation of redundant optional work under sustained queue residence.

## Novelty / overlap

Repository checks across open and closed issues for `Zeno`, `minimum inter-event`, `event separation`, `chattering`, `event storm`, and safety/event-trigger terms found no exact hypothesis combining (a) a lower bound on optional reassessment spacing, (b) a deadline derived from worst-case observation-to-physical-release latency and uncertainty growth, and (c) a hard immediate bypass lane for invalidation/revocation. Nearby work is substantial and must remain distinct: #5352 hysteresis; #6089 reachable-tube action/observation horizon; #5905 looming as a local-YIELD cue; #5317 prefix safety filter; #6650/#6710 persistence throttling and controller-law audit; #658/#668/#712/#1008/#1021 critical-event buffering/backpressure. This is a scoped repository search, not a claim of global novelty. External event-triggered control is explicit prior art; the contribution sought is a finite discrete interface scheduling discriminator, if one survives the overlap review.

## H / T / D / C / U

**H:** In a finite delayed-feedback model with noisy threshold-crossing risk, a deadline-constrained minimum-spacing policy will use fewer optional reassessments than an immediate-trigger policy while matching or improving hard-boundary violations, provided every hard invalidation bypasses pacing. When the minimum spacing and safe deadline are incompatible, explicit early YIELD will prevent the violation; it may reduce task progress.

**T (T0, pure finite model):** Enumerate a preregistered finite grid of risk-margin trajectories, uncertainty growth, capture+verification+dispatch+release latency, transient bursts, noisy threshold oscillation, sustained approach, delayed/missing measurements, and optional-service budgets. Compare fixed-period sampling, raw event-triggered sampling with no spacing bound, hysteresis-only (#5352-style comparator), and deadline-constrained spacing with hard bypass. A separate exhaustive reference enumerator scores all opportunities, release times, missed deadlines, optional event count, suppressed/unknown intervals, and bypass latency. No GUI, model, input, user data, or runtime change.

**D:** `PASS_METHOD_SCOPED` only if the candidate exactly matches the independent oracle on all enumerated rows, produces zero hard-bypass suppression, zero release after the modeled deadline when a bypass/yield path exists, fewer optional reassessments than raw triggering on the frozen noisy/transient corpus, and no more boundary violations than raw triggering or fixed-period control on every frozen hazard corpus. `FAIL` for any invariant/oracle discrepancy or a frozen counterexample with a hard event paced. `UNCERTAIN_NO_DISCRIMINATION` if no policy dominates on event cost versus boundary misses, or the result changes under the declared latency/uncertainty sensitivity range. This method result cannot justify a live safety claim.

**C:** A simple fixed period or #5352-style hysteresis may yield the same event reduction with a simpler contract; immediate triggering may be necessary when event arrivals themselves are reliable; uncertainty/latency bounds may be unavailable or too conservative; an explicit immediate YIELD may dominate pacing.

**U:** Authored finite trajectories, chosen bounds and risk abstractions may omit semantic target changes, non-looming hazards, bursty GUI event delivery, actual capture/release tails, and endogenous planner delay. No empirical distribution, GUI/task effect, user benefit, safety guarantee, or production cadence follows.

## Expected value, cost, risk

A scoped result would answer whether a lower event-rate bound can coexist with a derived response deadline under noisy risk signals, and whether impossible scheduling regions should be surfaced as YIELD instead of hidden in a heuristic. It may connect #14's interrupt policy and #59's live-control gap to the #6089/#5317 safety envelope without duplicating their mechanism. T0 is a small deterministic standard-library enumeration and independent audit; no model/GPU/GUI allocation is needed. Main risk is false confidence from a hand-authored plant: keep it explicitly method-only and require later measured tail latency plus independently meaningful hazard/effect evidence before any live transfer.

items.title: [GPT QA] Distillation safety exhaustion falls back to training on filtered images

labels.name: qa:chatgpt
labels.description: Issues discovered by automated ChatGPT QA review.

labels.name: category:security
labels.description: Authentication, authorization, trust, exposure, or safety-boundary failure.

labels.name: severity:critical
labels.description: Critical defect with catastrophic, safety, or security impact.

labels.name: source:user-journey-qa
labels.description: Originally discovered by the scheduled user/system journey QA review.

items.body:
## Finding
The supported distillation training journey defeats its own safety boundary when a batch cannot produce any safe/accepted images within the retry budget. After safety filtering rejects all generated candidates, `TeacherDataset.sample()` explicitly falls back to the last candidate batch "unfiltered" and feeds those images into training. This converts a safety-system failure/exhaustion condition into acceptance of the exact content the safety filter rejected.

## User/System Journey
1. A researcher starts the supported `projects/distill/train_student.py` online teacher-distillation path with safety enabled (the normal configuration).
2. `TeacherDataset.sample(batch_size)` generates legitimate teacher candidates through ComfyUI.
3. Each candidate is passed through `self.safety.check(...)`; unsafe candidates are excluded from `all_accepted_images` and recorded by the safety tracker.
4. The sampler retries to obtain enough acceptable images. A normal teacher/model/prompt combination can legitimately produce a retry window in which every candidate is rejected by the safety policy.
5. If no candidate survives, the post-retry fallback executes `if not all_accepted_images:` and appends every image from the last generated candidate batch without another safety gate, marking them `fallback_unfiltered=True`.
6. Those tensors are stacked into `images`, converted to `x_start`, and returned to `train()`, which immediately uses them as the target training batch.

This is reachable without impossible state or internal injection: it requires only that the configured teacher produce unsafe outputs for the bounded retry window, which is precisely the external-model failure mode the safety filter exists to contain. The same bypass exists whether grading is enabled or disabled because safety rejection occurs in both branches before the common fallback.

## Files in scope
- `projects/distill/train_student.py` — `TeacherDataset.sample()`, safety/grading retry loop, `if not all_accepted_images` fallback, returned `x_start` training batch.
- `projects/distill/safety_filter.py` — safety decision boundary whose rejected outputs are subsequently bypassed.
- `train()` — consumes the fallback batch directly for flow-matching/KD training.

## Expected behavior
Safety rejection must remain a hard invariant across retry exhaustion. If the sampler cannot produce a safe batch, it should fail/skip/defer the training step, quarantine the offending teacher/checkpoint, or otherwise recover without admitting content that the safety policy rejected. Disabling grading must not disable safety.

## Actual behavior
When all candidates are filtered, the code logs `Using last batch unfiltered`, copies the last rejected candidate batch into the accepted lists, and trains on it. The fallback therefore reverses the safety decision exactly when the safety system is under maximum pressure from repeated unsafe teacher outputs.

## Correction direction
Restore a non-bypassable safety boundary between external teacher generation and training data. Retry exhaustion may relax quality/grading requirements if intended, but must never relax a safety rejection. Separate grading fallback from safety eligibility so only safety-approved candidates can reach `x_start`; define an explicit bounded recovery path for a teacher/checkpoint that cannot produce safe material. Add regressions for all-unsafe batches with grading both enabled and disabled, proving no rejected image reaches the training tensor after retries are exhausted.

## Metadata
- QA-Agent: ChatGPT
- Reviewed-SHA: `2ae8f15ca923737fdcc14fa5dcbdb03b8b7b5ae0`
- Branch: `main`
- Severity: Critical
- Category: safety
- Review-Mode: user-journey-head
- QA-Fingerprint: `xiaden/ML-Experiments|safety|distill.TeacherDataset.sample|retry-exhaustion-reintroduces-safety-rejected-teacher-images-into-training`

items.title: Migrate auto-reset to Hermes credentialed requests without weakening safety guarantees
items.body:
## Summary

Migrate Codex auto-reset requests to Hermes-managed authentication without weakening the existing credit-selection, persisted idempotency, locking, cooldown, and audit guarantees.

Related: #28 covers usage queries and shared authentication integration. This issue owns reset-credit listing and consumption, including exhausted-account recovery.

## Proposed direction

Use `hermes_cli.plugin_provider_requests.credentialed_provider_request()` for reset-credit GET/POST requests and declare `requires_auth: [openai-codex]`. The current ChatGPT backend origins are allowlisted; the helper accepts JSON and custom headers and returns status/headers/body without exposing the token.

Remove direct credential-store reads from the Hermes-hosted auto-reset path. Retain the coordinator's transaction policy rather than replacing it with a superficially similar core helper.

## Current limitations / blockers

Checked in Hermes v0.22.5 and main at `afe3cbd817b7f5655e4172b442acf6fa7c9bb55d`; findings are based on source review, not live redemption tests.

1. **Exhausted pool credentials may be unavailable.** The request helper uses `resolve_codex_runtime_credentials()`. In pool-only setups, `_pool_codex_credential()` excludes entries with a future cooldown, and unresolved quota exhaustion can prevent the reset request from being sent. Auto-reset must work while the weekly quota is exhausted; the usage/reset endpoints must not inherit completions-quota exclusion. Determine whether an upstream supported request mode is needed. Do not bypass this by reading tokens or patching private core functions.
2. **The built-in redeem helper does not preserve our idempotency contract.** `agent.account_usage.redeem_codex_reset_credit()` creates a fresh request UUID for each invocation and accepts neither an external `redeem_request_id` nor a `credit_id`. It therefore cannot directly replace the coordinator, which persists an ID before POST and reuses it across uncertain retries/restarts, and selects the earliest-expiring credit itself.
3. **Eligibility policies differ.** The built-in helper guards on any fully exhausted window unless forced. Our policy uses an explicitly configured weekly-remaining threshold. Preserve that behavior; do not add 5h-trigger eligibility as part of this migration (#21 is separate).
4. **Caller/profile constraints matter.** The public request helper requires an installed-plugin calling frame and provider declaration, rejects custom gateway credentials, and does not follow redirects. Verify hook/thread invocation and account continuity across usage, credit listing, and consumption; independent credential resolution must not silently switch the account being reset.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reset-credit requests use Hermes-managed credentials, with no direct credential-file reads in the Hermes-hosted path.
- [ ] A supported path works with exhausted, pool-only Codex credentials; unresolved upstream blockers are documented rather than hidden by a file-read fallback.
- [ ] The same persisted request ID survives ambiguous responses, retries, and process restarts.
- [ ] Earliest-expiring credit selection, null-expiry ordering, weekly-only threshold semantics, and account continuity are preserved.
- [ ] Locking, cooldowns, success suppression, one-time notices, and privacy-minimized permanent audit history remain intact.
- [ ] Synthetic tests cover exhaustion, account selection, concurrent hooks, timeouts/ambiguous POSTs, restart recovery, and successful terminal transitions.
- [ ] Compatibility requirements and any required upstream changes are documented. No real reset credit is consumed in automated tests.

## References

items.title: [Skill] verifying-agent-memory-retrieval-safety
items.body:
## Skill Name

`verifying-agent-memory-retrieval-safety`

## Domain

Application Development

## Description

Verifies that an agent-memory retrieval path on CockroachDB preserves tenant and eligibility boundaries before vector ranking, uses a compatible embedding space, and has an inspectable query plan. Use when reviewing RAG or agent-memory schemas, retrieval SQL, vector indexes, governance-state filters, or safe-abstention behavior before release.

## Scope and Boundaries

**Included:**
- Inventory the memory table, vector column, vector index, and relational provenance constraints.
- Verify tenant/workspace and application-owned eligibility predicates execute in SQL before ranking.
- Verify queries cannot mix incompatible embedding spaces.
- Use non-executing `EXPLAIN` to identify the selected index, spans/full scans, and distribution.
- Check bounded `ORDER BY` vector-distance queries and require explicit abstention when no eligible candidate exists.
- Produce a redacted pass/fail report with evidence, limitations, and remediation recommendations.

**Excluded:**
- Executing remediations or modifying application data.
- Claiming semantic quality, tenant row authorization, or production scale from schema inspection alone.
- Automatically creating/dropping indexes or enabling row-level security.
- Running `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, which executes the inner statement.
- Inspecting or emitting raw embeddings, secrets, connection strings, or sensitive memory text.

## Expected Inputs and Outputs

**Inputs:**
- Memory table/schema and retrieval SQL or prepared-statement shape.
- Expected tenant, service/domain, governance/validity, and embedding-space boundaries.
- Read-only CockroachDB access capable of schema inspection and `EXPLAIN`.
- Optional expected index name and maximum candidate count.

**Outputs:**
- Boundary matrix showing which predicates are enforced in SQL versus the application.
- Vector/index inventory and non-executing query-plan observations.
- Findings for cross-tenant exposure, ineligible-state retrieval, embedding-space mixing, unbounded candidate sets, and missing abstention behavior.
- Redacted release decision: pass, pass-with-limitations, or fail, with exact evidence and follow-up actions.

## Safety Considerations

- Default to read-only metadata and `EXPLAIN`; never use `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`.
- Never select or reproduce embedding values, secrets, connection strings, or sensitive memory content.
- Do not infer row-level authorization from tenant predicates or composite foreign keys; distinguish query isolation, relationship integrity, grants, and RLS.
- Treat query-plan evidence from small or synthetic corpora as functional evidence, not a scale or latency claim.
- Require explicit user approval before any recommended DDL is executed, preferably after staging validation and rollback planning.

## CockroachDB Documentation References

- https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable/vector
- https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable/indexes
- https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable/sql-tuning-with-explain
- https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable/explain-analyze
- https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable/security-reference/authorization

## Use Case and Motivation

Agent-memory systems often treat vector similarity as authorization. That can retrieve another tenant's data, revoked or unreviewed memories, known failed outcomes, or vectors from an incompatible model space. Existing skills cover general SQL, transactions, and operational security, but none combines agent-memory eligibility boundaries with vector-plan verification and safe abstention.

This skill would help application developers, AI platform engineers, security reviewers, and SREs produce a repeatable, honest pre-release assessment without exposing memory contents or mutating the cluster. It is based on a reusable pattern validated while building an outcome-governed incident-memory application, but remains application-agnostic.

## Proposal Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this skill has not been proposed yet.
- [x] I have reviewed the Agent Skills Specification.
- [x] I have read the contributing guidelines.
- [x] The skill name follows naming conventions.
